function.name: think
function.description: Plan, reflect, or analyze before taking action. Use this tool before complex steps, to verify your previous actions, or to correct course. Highly recommended for multi-step tasks. Keep reasoning concise.

reasoning.description: Brief plan or reflection (≤100 words): what you are analyzing and what steps you will take next.

function.name: search_files
function.description: Search file contents with a regex pattern (target='content', default) or find files by name (target='files', glob pattern like '*.py'). Returns matches as file:line: text, or a file list / match counts. Far more token-efficient than running grep/rg/find via execute_command. Constrained to 'path' (default '.'); never search from /.

pattern.description: Regex to search for (content) or filename glob (files target, e.g. '*.md').

path.description: Directory or file to search in (default current dir).

target.description: 'content' searches inside files (default); 'files' finds files by name.

file_glob.description: Only search files matching this glob (content target), e.g. '*.py'.

output_mode.description: 'content' (default) shows matching lines; 'files_only' lists files; 'count' shows per-file match counts.

function.name: todo
function.description: Maintain a task list for multi-step work (3+ steps). Call with NO arguments to read the current list. Pass a 'todos' array of {id, content, status} objects to create it (merge=false, default) or update existing items by id (merge=true). status is one of: pending, in_progress, completed, cancelled. Mark items completed immediately when done; only ONE item in_progress at a time. The list persists to disk so it survives interruptions.

todos.description: Task items. Omit entirely to read the current list.

merge.description: true: update existing items by id and add new ones. false (default): replace the whole list.

function.name: clarify
function.description: Ask the user a question and wait for their answer before continuing. Use when the task is ambiguous and a wrong guess wastes real work: give 2-4 numbered 'choices' (first = recommended; the user can also type their own). Omit choices for an open-ended question. In non-interactive runs (bridges, schedulers) it returns a note telling you to pick a sensible default and proceed — never block waiting for a human.

question.description: The question itself (no options inside the text).

choices.description: Up to 4 options as separate strings; the user picks one or types their own. Put the recommended option FIRST.

multi_select.description: true: user may pick several options.

timeout_seconds.description: Optional: give up waiting after N seconds and proceed with a default.

function.name: browser
function.description: Drive a persistent headless Chromium browser for JS-only sites, forms and interactive pages (fetch_webpage cannot do these). Actions: goto(url), content(), html(), links(), click(selector), fill(selector, value), select(selector, value), press(key), js(expr), wait(selector?), back(), screenshot(path?), status(), shutdown. Page state (current URL, inputs, JS context) persists across browser calls. For a plain static page prefer fetch_webpage — it is faster.

expr.description: For js: a JS expression to evaluate.

wait_ms.description: Timeout in ms for the action.

path.description: For screenshot: where to save the PNG.

function.name: spawn_agent
function.description: Register a named persistent agent (stored under ~/.config/ai/agents). Use together with resume_agent to run a recurring helper agent that keeps its own conversation history across invocations. For one-shot parallel work prefer delegate_task instead.

prompt.description: What the agent is for (stored as its mission).

budget.description: Optional thinking token budget for reasoning (e.g. 2048, 4096, 8192).

function.name: resume_agent
function.description: Send a message to a previously spawned agent (agent_id from spawn_agent/list_agents) and return its response. The agent's history persists on disk between resumes.

message.description: The user message for this turn.

budget.description: Optional reasoning thinking token budget override for this turn.

function.name: list_agents
function.description: List all registered agents (id, name, status, mission). Read-only.

function.name: append_to_context_pool
function.description: Store a snippet of context in the shared pool that persists across agents/sessions (e.g. a key finding, a decision, a path). Other agents and future sessions can retrieve it with search_context / get_context_snippet.

function.name: search_context
function.description: Search the shared context pool (from append_to_context_pool and command output) for an entry containing the query. Read-only.

function.name: get_context_snippet
function.description: Fetch one stored context-pool entry by its numeric index. Read-only.

function.name: structured_query
function.description: Query a file or command output like a pipeline: target='file:/path' or 'command:ls -la', plus filter (regex), transform (head:N | tail:N | sort | unique), aggregate (count | first | last). Use to count/grep/summarise without writing a script.

function.name: session_report
function.description: Log the outcome of this session (success bool, failure modes, notes) to ~/.config/ai/session_outcomes.json. Call near task_complete for non-trivial sessions so the self-improvement loop has outcome data.

success.description: Did the session achieve its goal?

function.name: execute_command
function.description: Run a shell command on the host system and return its stdout and stderr. Use for any system task, file inspection, or quick scripts. IMPORTANT: For long-running tasks (e.g. training, servers, heavy builds), DO NOT use this tool as it blocks the main thread and locks the GUI. Instead, use `start_background_process` to detach the job so you can monitor or stop it if needed.

command.description: The exact shell command to execute.

timeout.description: Optional timeout in seconds. Defaults to 120s. For tasks requiring more than a few minutes, use `start_background_process` instead.

function.name: python_playground
function.description: Execute a snippet of Python code in an isolated interactive sandbox. Returns evaluated expressions, print outputs, and exceptions without leaving scratch files on disk.

code.description: The Python code or expression to run in the playground.

function.name: js_playground
function.description: Execute a snippet of JavaScript / Node.js in an isolated sandbox. Returns console outputs and evaluated expressions without leaving scratch files on disk.

code.description: The JavaScript code or expression to run in the playground.

function.name: execute_remote_command
function.description: Run a command on a remote host via SSH. You must have passwordless SSH access (e.g. key-based) already configured for the host.

host.description: The SSH host (e.g., user@hostname or just hostname).

command.description: The bash command to run remotely.

function.name: remote_exec
function.description: Remote Server Control Tool. Connect, discover, execute commands, monitor resources, submit jobs on a remote server cluster. Supports connection lifecycle management, auto-discovery of compute nodes, HPC job submission (Slurm/PBS/Torque), and resource monitoring.

action.description: Action to perform: connect, disconnect, discover, status, exec, mount, jobs, submit

host.description: Remote server hostname or IP (required for connect)

command.description: Command to execute (required for exec, submit)

function.name: web_search
function.description: Search the web using DuckDuckGo to find current information, prices, news, documentation, or facts you don't know. Always follow with fetch_webpage on at least one result URL before calling task_complete.

function.name: arxiv_search
function.description: Search the arXiv API for scientific papers. Returns metadata and abstracts.

max_results.description: Max number of results to return (default 5, max 10).

function.name: fetch_webpage
function.description: Download and read any URL. This is the robust default: it uses a browser TLS fingerprint (curl_cffi) to get past Cloudflare and bot-walls, and auto-escalates to a headless browser for JS-rendered pages when needed. Use it for essentially every page. Required before task_complete if search returned URLs — never present links without reading them.

url.description: The URL of the webpage to fetch.

function.name: fetch_smart
function.description: Preferred fetch tool. Downloads a URL using browser TLS fingerprint impersonation (curl_cffi) to bypass Cloudflare and similar bot protections. Automatically escalates to Playwright+stealth for JS-rendered pages if the fast path is blocked. Use this for any URL that might be protected, JS-heavy, or from a news/media site. Falls back to fetch_webpage if curl_cffi is not installed.

function.name: read_file
function.description: Read the contents of a file. Supports text files, PDFs (extracts text), and image files (PNG, JPG, JPEG, WEBP) which are shown in context. For large text files an outline + head/tail is returned automatically. Use start_line and end_line to read a specific section of a large file.

path.description: The path to the file to read.

start_line.description: First line to return (1-based, inclusive). Omit to start from the beginning.

end_line.description: Last line to return (1-based, inclusive). Omit to read to the end.

function.name: write_file
function.description: Write content to a file, creating it and any parent directories if needed. After writing a script, always run it with execute_command to verify it works.

path.description: The path to the file to write to.

content.description: The exact content to write to the file.

function.name: edit_file
function.description: Apply a search-and-replace edit to an existing file. The search_content must match exactly including whitespace.

path.description: The path to the file to edit.

search_content.description: The exact text block to search for and replace.

function.name: patch_file
function.description: Atomically apply one or multiple search-and-replace hunks to a file with fuzzy whitespace matching. If any hunk fails to match, no changes are written.

path.description: The path to the file to patch.

hunks.description: Array of {search, replace} objects to apply in order.

search.description: Single search chunk if not using hunks.

replace.description: Single replace chunk if not using hunks.

function.name: get_environment
function.description: Get detailed runtime environment info: OS, Python version, working directory, git branch/status, GPU model and memory usage, and backend model settings.

function.name: list_directory
function.description: List the contents of a directory on the host system. Use to explore project structure before reading specific files.

path.description: The path to the directory to list. Defaults to '.' if not specified.

function.name: save_memory
function.description: Add key facts, user preferences, or context to persistent memory (appended; duplicates skipped; oldest lines evicted past 4 KB). This memory is automatically loaded in subsequent runs.

content.description: The fact(s) to add, one per line. Keep it concise.

replace.description: Rewrite the whole memory with content instead of appending (use only to clean up or correct it).

function.name: remember
function.description: Save key facts, user preferences, or context to long-term persistent memory using SQLite FTS5 full-text search. Memories can be later retrieved via the 'recall' tool.

content.description: The exact content to store in memory. Keep it concise.

function.name: recall
function.description: Search long-term memories using natural language full-text search (SQLite FTS5). Returns matching saved memories.

query.description: The search query — can be a word, phrase, or FTS5 boolean expression.

function.name: list_processes
function.description: Return the top 10 running processes sorted by CPU usage.

function.name: start_background_process
function.description: Start a command in the background, writing stdout/stderr output to a log file for status & health monitoring.

command.description: The command line string to run asynchronously in background.

log_file.description: Optional log file path. Defaults to ~/.config/ai/logs/proc_<timestamp>.log if omitted.

function.name: check_process_status
function.description: Inspect a background process state, read recent log output, evaluate health status, and receive a decision summary.

pid.description: PID of the background process to inspect.

log_file.description: Path to the log file to inspect.

function.name: stop_process
function.description: Terminate a running background process by PID.

pid.description: PID of the process to terminate.

function.name: delegate_task
function.description: Spawn N helper agents that run IN PARALLEL and return their combined results. Use ONLY for independent sub-tasks (each agent must not depend on another's output). Always pass 'tasks' as an array — even for a single task. Example: fetch and summarise 3 papers → tasks:["Fetch https://... and summarise", "Fetch https://... and summarise", ...]. Each task string must be fully self-contained with all context (URLs, file paths, goals). For fetching multiple URLs, prefer parallel_fetch instead — it is faster and needs no per-URL instructions.

tasks.description: Array of self-contained task instructions. Each runs in its own agent concurrently.

budget.description: Optional thinking token budget per helper agent (e.g. 2048, 4096).

function.name: parallel_fetch
function.description: Fetch multiple URLs concurrently and return all page contents in one call. Use instead of multiple sequential fetch_webpage calls whenever you need 2+ pages. Example use cases: reading several search results, fetching multiple papers/docs, multi-site comparison, publication digest. Each result is capped at 10 KB and labelled with its URL.

urls.description: List of URLs to fetch concurrently.

function.name: load_skill
function.description: Explore and load domain skills. Call with no argument (empty name) to list all available skills with descriptions. Call with a skill name to read its full guidance. Always call with no argument first if you are unsure what skills exist, then load the relevant one before starting domain work.

name.description: Skill directory name to load (e.g. 'bio_structure_analysis'). Omit or leave empty to list all available skills.

function.name: fetch_webpage_js
function.description: Explicit Playwright override: renders the page with a real headless browser + stealth patches (playwright-stealth, realistic 1920×1080 viewport, lazy-load scroll). Use only when you need direct control over JS rendering or wait_for behaviour. For most cases, prefer fetch_smart which cascades automatically.

url.description: The URL to fetch with a headless browser.

wait_for.description: When to consider the page ready. 'networkidle' (default) waits for no network activity — best for SPAs. 'load' waits for the load event. 'domcontentloaded' is fastest but may miss late-rendered content.

function.name: get_system_status
function.description: Return a compact one-line summary of CPU usage, RAM, and disk. Useful for quickly checking system resources before running heavy operations.

function.name: get_clipboard
function.description: Read the current system clipboard content (X11 via xclip or Wayland via wl-paste). Returns the plain text currently on the clipboard, or an error if nothing is available.

function.name: learn_rule
function.description: Save a permanent system rule or constraint to your dynamic rules file. These rules are injected into your system prompt on all future runs.

rule_text.description: The exact text of the rule to learn.

function.name: reset_context
function.description: Clear your conversational history to prevent context window bloat. Use this after completing a sub-task or when transitioning to a new topic to regain full reasoning capacity.

function.name: vault_write
function.description: Create or update a Markdown note in the Obsidian Graph Vault. Used to store long-term structured knowledge, agentic state, and plans.

title.description: The title of the note (will become the filename).

content.description: The Markdown content of the note.

links.description: Optional comma-separated list of other note titles to link to (e.g. 'Project Alpha, Database Schema').

function.name: vault_read
function.description: Read the full Markdown content of a specific note from the Graph Vault.

function.name: vault_search
function.description: Perform a full-text FTS5 search across all notes in the Graph Vault.

function.name: vault_backlinks
function.description: Traverse the Knowledge Graph by finding all notes that link to (mention) a specific note title via [[WikiLinks]].

function.name: pubmed_search
function.description: Semantic search across 50M+ biomedical abstracts (PubMed, BioRxiv, MedRxiv, arXiv). Returns titles, authors, journals, DOIs, abstracts, and relevance scores. Use iteratively: search → digest abstracts → refine query → search again → synthesise. Always report DOIs so manuscripts can be retrieved. Requires PUBMED_API_KEY (or MSS_API_KEY) environment variable.

query.description: Natural-language search query (3–500 chars), e.g. 'CRISPR base editing off-target effects'.

top_k.description: Number of results to return (5–10, default 10).

start_date.description: Restrict to papers published on or after this date (YYYY-MM-DD). Optional.

end_date.description: Restrict to papers published on or before this date (YYYY-MM-DD). Optional.

high_quality_only.description: Exclude papers with missing or very short abstracts (default true).

function.name: gcal_list_events
function.description: List events from Google Calendar in a specified time range.

time_min.description: Start time in ISO 8601 format (e.g. '2026-07-01T00:00:00-06:00' or '2026-07-01T00:00:00Z'). Defaults to current time.

time_max.description: End time in ISO 8601 format. Defaults to 7 days from start time.

max_results.description: Maximum number of events to return. Defaults to 20.

calendar_ids.description: Optional list of calendar IDs to search. Omit or set to ['all'] to search all of your selected Google calendars.

function.name: gcal_create_event
function.description: Create a new event in Google Calendar with exact start/end times. For natural-language phrases ('lunch with Sam tomorrow 1pm'), prefer gcal_quick_add instead.

start_time.description: Start time, ISO 8601 (e.g. '2026-07-01T14:00:00'). A timezone offset is optional — without one it is interpreted in the user's local timezone (or the time_zone arg). Use a bare date ('2026-07-01') for an all-day event.

end_time.description: End time, ISO 8601 (e.g. '2026-07-01T15:00:00'). Offset optional. Use a bare date for all-day events.

time_zone.description: Optional IANA timezone name (e.g. 'America/New_York') for naive start/end times. Defaults to the system local timezone.

description.description: Optional detailed description of the event.

calendar_id.description: Optional ID of the calendar to create the event in. Defaults to 'primary' (your main calendar).

function.name: gcal_check_availability
function.description: Check free/busy time slots for Google Calendar to query availability.

calendar_ids.description: Optional list of calendar IDs to check. Defaults to ['primary'].

function.name: gcal_quick_add
function.description: Create a Google Calendar event from a natural-language phrase — Google parses the date/time/title for you. Best default for casual event creation, e.g. 'Dentist appointment next Tuesday at 3pm' or 'Lunch with Sam tomorrow 12-1pm'.

text.description: Natural-language description including when and what, e.g. 'Team sync Friday 10am'.

function.name: gcal_update_event
function.description: Reschedule or modify an existing Google Calendar event. Only the fields you pass are changed. Call gcal_list_events first to get the event_id.

event_id.description: ID of the event to update (from gcal_list_events).

start_time.description: New start time, ISO 8601 (optional). Offset optional; naive times use time_zone or local tz.

time_zone.description: Optional IANA timezone for naive start/end times.

function.name: gcal_delete_event
function.description: Cancel/delete a Google Calendar event by its ID. Call gcal_list_events first to get the event_id. This is irreversible.

event_id.description: ID of the event to delete (from gcal_list_events).

function.name: check_time
function.description: Returns the current local date, time, and day of the week.

function.name: schedule_task
function.description: MANDATORY replacement for `sleep` delays. NEVER use execute_command with sleep for timed work — it blocks the terminal and the Zulip bridge, hanging the session with no response. Use this tool instead for ANY deferred, timed, or periodic work: desktop notifications, reminders, polling folders, checking job status, sending messages when a condition is met. This returns IMMEDIATELY — the task runs in a fully detached background process. IMPORTANT: Every polling task MUST have an explicit termination condition. Always set max_runs (e.g. 20) OR ttl_hours (e.g. 4.0) as a safety guardrail in case the sub-agent never calls unschedule_task — this prevents orphaned background tasks. For ONE-SHOT tasks: use run_once=True (guaranteed single execution, no agent needed) or end the prompt with 'then call unschedule_task(task_id)'. For POLLING tasks: include the unschedule_task call in the agent prompt AND set max_runs. After calling this, immediately call task_complete to confirm the schedule to the user.

task_id.description: A unique snake_case identifier, e.g. 'notify_go_home' or 'check_binders_done'.

prompt.description: Full self-contained instruction for the background agent. Must include everything it needs. For polling: always end with 'If done, call unschedule_task(task_id). Else do nothing.' Example one-shot: 'Run: execute_command("notify-send \"Go home!\" \"Time to leave 🏠\""); then call unschedule_task(notify_go_home).' Example polling: 'Count files in /data/results. If count >= 10000: send Zulip private message to user@example.com saying how many passed filters; then call unschedule_task(check_binders). Else do nothing.'

interval_seconds.description: How often to run (minimum 10s). For one-shot reminders, set this to the full delay (e.g. 300 for 5 minutes). For polling, set to a shorter check interval (e.g. 120 for every 2 min).

run_once.description: If true, the task is guaranteed to run exactly once after interval_seconds and then stop — no matter what the sub-agent does. Use this for simple one-shot reminders/notifications instead of relying on the sub-agent to call unschedule_task. Default is false.

max_runs.description: Safety cap: automatically cancel the task after this many agent invocations, regardless of whether unschedule_task was called. Use 0 (default) for unlimited. STRONGLY RECOMMENDED for all polling tasks — set to the maximum reasonable number of checks (e.g. 20 for a task polling every 5min over ~2h). Prevents orphaned tasks if the agent never calls unschedule_task.

ttl_hours.description: Safety expiry: automatically cancel the task after this many hours since creation, regardless of run count. Use 0 (default) for unlimited. STRONGLY RECOMMENDED as a backstop (e.g. 4.0 for a task expected to finish in ~2h). Prevents orphaned tasks from surviving across reboots or multi-day runs.

function.name: set_reminder
function.description: Set a one-shot reminder that is delivered straight to Zulip at a future time — use this for 'remind me tomorrow to ...', 'ping me in 2 hours to ...', etc. Preferred over schedule_task for reminders: delivery is deterministic (no LLM run) so it can't be garbled. Convert natural phrases like 'tomorrow 9am' into an ISO timestamp yourself using the current local time from the system context, and pass it as `when`. When the request comes from Zulip chat, the recipient is filled in automatically — you only need `message` and `when`. After calling this, call task_complete to confirm.

message.description: The reminder text to send back to the user, e.g. 'Submit the grant report'.

when.description: Absolute delivery time as an ISO 8601 timestamp, e.g. '2026-07-05T09:00:00'. Convert 'tomorrow 9am' etc. yourself from the current time. Provide this OR delay_seconds.

delay_seconds.description: Alternative to `when`: how many seconds from now to fire (e.g. 7200 for 2 hours).

zulip_to.description: Recipient email for a Zulip DM. Optional — from the Zulip bridge this defaults to the requester automatically.

zulip_stream.description: Alternatively, a Zulip stream/channel name to post the reminder to.

zulip_topic.description: Topic for the stream message (defaults to 'Reminders'). Only used with zulip_stream.

function.name: unschedule_task
function.description: Cancel a previously scheduled background task and stop its recurring execution.

task_id.description: The unique identifier of the task to cancel/stop.

function.name: list_scheduled_tasks
function.description: List all currently scheduled background tasks with their ID, prompt, interval, and last run time.

function.name: present_plan
function.description: PLAN MODE: Investigate first, then present your findings and the ordered list of exact changes you intend to make, and wait for approval before making ANY change. Call this before modifying state (write/edit files, run state-changing commands, save memory, schedule, delegate subagents, etc.). On approval you get a BOUNDED number of state-changing actions (INFER_PLAN_STEP_BUDGET, default 8): execute those steps ONE at a time, validate each result, and when the budget is exhausted call present_plan again with the next chunk. Never start a new change without an in-force approval. The user approves or rejects; do NOT proceed with changes until approved.

plan.description: Your findings so far, the exact changes or commands you intend to run, and your reasoning / suggestions. Be concrete.

function.name: search_history
function.description: Search all past conversations (backed up locally) with full-text search. Use this to learn from earlier sessions — recall how a previous problem was solved, which commands worked, what the user asked before, etc. Returns matched snippets + session IDs; then call get_session to read a full conversation.

query.description: Keywords to find in past conversations.

function.name: list_sessions
function.description: List the most recent backed-up conversations (session id, size, path). Use it to see what you've worked on recently or to find a session_id for get_session.

limit.description: Number of recent sessions to list (default 12).

function.name: get_session
function.description: Load a full backed-up conversation by session_id as a readable transcript. Use after search_history / list_sessions to read the entire prior conversation in context.

function.name: rebuild_history_index
function.description: Rebuild the full-text search index over all backed-up conversations. Normally automatic; call if history search seems stale or returned nothing.

function.name: search_zulip_chats
function.description: Search and inspect past Zulip chat interactions stored in persistent Zulip memory. Returns timestamp, status, duration, query snippets, and error traces. Use this to investigate Zulip issues, recall recent Zulip discussions, or troubleshoot bridge errors.

query.description: Optional keyword or session_id to search in Zulip chat history.

error_only.description: If true, only return chats that ended in error, fallback, or empty output.

function.name: get_zulip_chat
function.description: Load the complete, raw JSON log for a specific Zulip interaction by its session_id (including prompt sent to model, stdout, stderr, delivered reply, and timing).

function.name: skill_create
function.description: SELF-IMPROVEMENT: Persist what you learned during this session into a reusable skill so future sessions inherit it. Call this after completing a non-trivial task, discovering a useful technique/workaround, or when a skill states something you found to be wrong. Saved to the repo .agents/skills AND ~/.config/ai/skills. The user is notified when a skill is created.

description.description: One-line description: when to use this skill.

content.description: Full skill body: numbered steps, exact commands, pitfalls, verification, sources.

function.name: skill_update
function.description: SELF-IMPROVEMENT: Add a 'good to know' note or discrepancy fix to an existing skill after you loaded it and learned something new or found it wrong/outdated. The user is notified when a skill is updated.

name.description: Name of the existing skill to update.

note.description: Concise note: what to fix / what you learned, with any exact command or correction.

function.name: skill_note
function.description: SELF-IMPROVEMENT: Append a standalone learning note to the persisted skills learning log without editing any skill body. Lower-commitment than skill_create/update.

name.description: Optional skill name to associate the note with.

note.description: The lesson / insight to remember across sessions.

function.name: task_complete
function.description: Call this ONLY when you have the verified answer from tools. Write the full result in summary — this is the only output the user sees. Do not call this if you still have URLs to fetch, commands to run, or scripts to verify.

summary.description: The complete answer or result for the user, in markdown. Include all relevant data you gathered from tools.
